summary: Request timeouts for long-context prompts and high max_tokens on hosted API
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports repeated request timeouts when sending long-context prompts (>60k tokens) or using large max_tokens values (>=2048) to our hosted text-generation endpoint. Timeouts occur after ~60s and manifest as HTTP 504 / streaming disconnects.

Impact:
- Affected customer: DocuAssist (enterprise) has production traffic blocked for a feature that uses long-context summarization.
- Error rate for their API key spiked to ~18% on 2026-03-01 between 02:10-03:40 UTC.
- Business impact: feature is degraded for end users; customer requests urgent mitigation.

Environment:
- Hosted API (api.redwood.ai) in us-east region.
- Customer pinned to redwood-13b model via model_version field.

Steps to reproduce:
1) POST /v1/generate with model=redwood-13b and prompt with ~60k tokens of concatenated documents.
2) Set max_tokens=2048 and stream=true.
3) Observe request stalls and returns HTTP 504 after ~60s, or the streaming connection drops with no final token.

Observed behavior:
- Upstream request times out at ~60s with 504 Gateway Timeout in the API layer.
- Serving runtime logs show repeated "kv_cache_eviction" and "batch_recompile" messages around same timestamp.
- Memory spikes on several serving nodes and GPU utilization jumps then drops as processes OOM-kill or are preempted.

Expected behavior:
- Reasonable backpressure/queueing behavior instead of client-visible 504s for long contextual requests, or clear 429s when exceeding configured resource limits.

Logs and traces (high-level):
- API gateway logs (trace id 1a2b3c) show upstream returned 504 at 2026-03-01T02:19:36Z.
- Serving-runtime logs show repeated "kv_cache_eviction" and "batch_recompile" messages around same timestamp.
- SRE dashboard (Latency by sequence length) shows P95 token latency regressed from 180ms to 2.1s for long-context buckets on 2026-03-01.

Immediate mitigation/workaround applied:
- Support temporarily routed DocuAssist traffic to a dedicated warm pool with higher memory headroom.
- Increased API gateway timeout for the customer's route to 120s as a stop-gap.
- Added request throttling on extremely long single-request sequences to prevent single-job resource exhaustion.

Next steps (in-progress):
- Engineering (serving-runtime) investigating batch heuristics and KV cache eviction policies for long contexts.
- Product to propose limits and SDK guidance for customers using very long contexts.
- SRE to create an alert for memory-pressure correlated to sequence-length buckets.

investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Long-context requests cause excessive KV cache churn and trigger batch recompilation which stalls token generation while blocking other batches.
Hypothesis 2: Default API gateway upstream timeout (60s) exposes long tail for very large max_tokens; serving runtime may continue generating but gateway gives up.
Finding: Reproduction confirms serving runtime sometimes continues generation beyond 60s but api-gateway returns 504 because forwarding response is delayed by batch recompile and memory thrashing.
Telemetry: P95 latency for sequences >50k tokens increased by 10x on 2026-03-01; correlated with spike in "kv_cache_eviction" events across us-east serving pool.
Repro steps created for engineering with fixture payloads and request_ids; attached to INT-4021 and PR 981 for runtime patch proposals.
resolution: Mitigation applied: customer traffic routed to a dedicated warm pool and API gateway timeout increased to 120s. Additionally enabled soft-throttling for single-request sequence length >50k tokens to protect shared pool. Engineering to roll runtime patch to improve batching heuristics and KV cache eviction (tracked in INT-4021 and PR 981). Postmortem and permanent config changes pending.
workaround_instructions: If you see 504s on long-context requests: 1) Reduce max_tokens or split input across multiple requests and use progressive summarization. 2) Set stream=false for extremely large outputs to reduce connection sensitivity. 3) Contact support to request routing to a dedicated warm pool while we investigate.
